raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "tomviz" %}
{% set version = "3.1.0" %}
{% set paraview_version = "6.1.1" %}
{% set build_number = 0 %}

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}-split
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  - git_url: https://github.com/OpenChemistry/tomviz
    git_rev: {{ version }}
    folder: tomviz
  # Submodules updated in build.sh: pybind11
  # conda-fixes.patch was dropped for 3.0: every hunk is now upstream, or
  # targeted a file that no longer exists.

build:
  number: {{ build_number }}

outputs:
  # First output: main tomviz desktop application
  - name: tomviz
    script: build_tomviz.sh   # [unix]
    script: build_tomviz.bat  # [win]
    build:
      number: {{ build_number }}
      # py310 is skipped: the paraview 6.1.1 py310 osx-64 package is broken
      # (missing jsoncpp symbol at import time)
      skip: true  # [py < 311]
    requirements:
      build:
        - {{ compiler('c') }}
        - {{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - {{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cmake
        - ninja
        - git
      host:
        - python
        - paraview =={{ paraview_version }}
        - vtk
        - tbb-devel
        - libxml2-devel
        - libprotobuf
        # Not linked by tomviz itself either: paraview's vtkRemotingApplication
        # links libhdf5 but paraview declares no hdf5 run dependency, so without
        # this run_export the solver pairs paraview (hdf5 1.14) with the hdf5 2
        # builds of vtk-base and h5py and `import paraview.simple` fails with
        # "Library not loaded: @rpath/libhdf5.310.dylib". Also enrolls this
        # feedstock in the hdf5 migration so it rebuilds when paraview does.
        - hdf5
      run:
        - python
        # The pipeline library now lives in openchemistry/tomviz-pipeline and
        # ships from its own feedstock; the app requires >=3.1.3,<4.
        - tomviz-pipeline >=3.1.3,<4
        - numpy
        - scipy
        - h5py
        - click
        - tqdm
        - marshmallow
        - jsonpatch
        - jsonpointer
        - pyfftw
        - pygments
    test:
      imports:
        - paraview
        - paraview.simple
        - paraview.numpy_support
        - tomviz
        - tomviz_pipeline
        - tomviz._realtime.ctvlib
      commands:
        - tomviz-pipeline --help
        - test -f $PREFIX/bin/tomviz  # [unix]
        - test -f $PREFIX/lib/libtomvizcore${SHLIB_EXT}  # [unix]
        - "! ldd $PREFIX/bin/tomviz | grep 'not found'"  # [linux]
        - "! ldd $PREFIX/lib/libtomvizcore${SHLIB_EXT} | grep 'not found'"  # [linux]
        - "! otool -L $PREFIX/bin/tomviz | grep 'not found'"  # [osx]
        - "! otool -L $PREFIX/lib/libtomvizcore${SHLIB_EXT} | grep 'not found'"  # [osx]
        - "timeout 20 tomviz || test $? -eq 124"  # [osx]
        - if not exist %LIBRARY_BIN%\\tomviz.exe exit 1  # [win]
        - if not exist %LIBRARY_BIN%\\tomvizcore.dll exit 1  # [win]
        - powershell -Command "$p = Start-Process tomviz -PassThru; Start-Sleep 20; if ($p.HasExited) { exit 1 } else { Stop-Process $p; exit 0 }"  # [win]
      requires:
        - coreutils  # [osx]
    about:
      home: https://github.com/OpenChemistry/tomviz
      license: BSD-3-Clause
      license_family: BSD
      license_file:
        - tomviz/LICENSE
      summary: 'Cross platform, open source application for the processing, visualization, and analysis of 3D tomography data'
      doc_url: https://tomviz.readthedocs.io/
      dev_url: https://github.com/OpenChemistry/tomviz

# This extra "about" section is a requirement by conda-forge, even
# though it's not actually used.
about:
  home: https://github.com/OpenChemistry/tomviz
  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_family: BSD
  license_file:
    - tomviz/LICENSE
  summary: 'Cross platform, open source application for the processing, visualization, and analysis of 3D tomography data'
  doc_url: https://tomviz.readthedocs.io/
  dev_url: https://github.com/OpenChemistry/tomviz

extra:
  feedstock-name: tomviz
  recipe-maintainers:
    - cjh1
    - psavery
    - conda-forge/event-model
